inputs.prompt: One original Bellwake Oars human fighter, brown swept-back tied hair, pale face looking RIGHT, grey shoulder cape and layered grey tunic, white neck scarf and torn white cloth streamers, dark grey trousers, brown strapped boots, leather belts and small bronze waist bells. Exactly TWO arms, TWO hands and TWO legs. Both hands grip ONE long rigid dark pole-oar diagonally: screen-left hand holds the upper shaft near shoulder, screen-right hand holds the lower shaft near waist. One small brass hanging bell and white tassels at the upper-left end, one broad dark leaf-shaped paddle blade with a gold curved tip at the lower-right end. Keep the complete oar length, blade shape, bells, both hands and unchanged spaced grips throughout; no extra staff, duplicate blade or weapon swap. Locked orthographic three-quarter game camera, facing RIGHT throughout, constant original body scale, full body and long oar inside generous frame margins, stable ground baseline, no zoom or turn away. Solid uniform saturated BLUE chroma-key background remains edge-to-edge unchanged for every frame; no black bars, fade, wipe or scenery. One simple two-handed forward thrust of the intact rigid oar. From the original diagonal ready stance, draw both elbows slightly backward for anticipation, then rotate the whole straight shaft as one solid piece into a horizontal rightward thrust at chest height. Both hands remain closed around the same spaced points on the shaft. The upper-left bell stays firmly connected to the butt of the same shaft and the broad paddle blade stays at its right end. Lean into a supported rightward knee lunge matching the supplied contact pose. Withdraw both hands and the entire straight oar together, return to the original diagonal ready stance. One compact attack with readable anticipation, thrust, contact and recovery. Do not lift the weapon overhead. No broken shaft, floating bell, weapon spin, loose hands, crossing hands, duplicate weapon, magic, trails or particles.
